run-a-program.question: What does print("Hello") show in the terminal?
run-a-program.explanation: The quotation marks delimit the string in the source; they are not part of the output.

values-and-names.question: What do 7 // 2 and 7 % 2 produce?
values-and-names.explanation: // is floor division, giving 3; % gives the remainder, 1.

text-and-input.question: name = "  Ada " is followed by a line containing only name.strip(). What is len(name) afterwards?
text-and-input.explanation: Strings do not change in place. strip returns a new string, and this code never assigns it, so name still has 6 characters.

conditions.question: With score = 50, which branch runs in: if score > 50 … elif score >= 50 … else …?
conditions.explanation: 50 > 50 is false and 50 >= 50 is true, so the elif branch is the first match. Boundary values show the difference between > and >=.

collections.question: first = [1, 2]; second = first; second.append(3). What is first now?
collections.explanation: second = first gives the same list a second name, so appending through either name changes that one list. Use first.copy() for an independent list.

loops.question: In for index, label in enumerate(["a", "b"]), what is index when label is "b"?
loops.explanation: enumerate counts from zero, so "a" pairs with 0 and "b" with 1.

functions.question: def add(item, items=[]): items.append(item); return items. After add(1), what does add(2) return?
functions.explanation: The default list is created once, when the function is defined, so both calls append to the same list. Use None as the default and create a list inside the function.

errors.question: Why avoid a bare except: around a calculation?
options: It can hide programming errors and interrupt signals
Python refuses to run a bare except
It makes every call noticeably slower
errors.explanation: A bare except catches everything, including mistakes you need to see and KeyboardInterrupt. Catch the narrow exception you know how to handle.

files-and-json.question: What does json.loads(json.dumps({1: "a"})) return?
files-and-json.explanation: JSON object keys are always strings, so the integer key 1 comes back as the string '1'.

modules-and-environments.question: What does if __name__ == "__main__": stop from happening?
options: Script entry code running when the file is imported
modules-and-environments.explanation: The guarded block runs only when the file is executed directly, so importing its functions does not also run the program.

testing-and-api-boundaries.question: A test calls the parser and prints the result. What is it missing?
options: An assertion that checks the expected value
A live request to the real service
testing-and-api-boundaries.explanation: Printing does not check anything; the test passes whatever the parser returns. An assertion states the expected behavior.

study-log-capstone.question: For the first version of the study log, which data structure is enough?
options: A class hierarchy for each record type
study-log-capstone.explanation: A list of dictionaries holds topic and minutes records. A class is optional, and a database is beyond this one-process version.

classes-and-dataclasses.question: Why write items: list = field(default_factory=list) in a dataclass?
options: Each instance gets its own new list
It checks that the list holds only integers
It freezes the list after construction
classes-and-dataclasses.explanation: default_factory calls list() for every new instance. A plain = [] default is rejected because one list would be shared.

typing-and-protocols.question: A class has every method a Protocol requires but does not inherit from it. Does a static checker accept it where the Protocol is expected?
options: No; it must subclass the Protocol
Yes; protocols are matched by structure
Only when the Protocol is runtime_checkable
typing-and-protocols.explanation: Protocols describe required operations, so any object that provides them fits. runtime_checkable only affects isinstance checks.

iterators-and-generators.question: When does the body of a generator function start running?
options: When iteration asks for the first value
iterators-and-generators.explanation: Calling a generator function only creates the generator object. Its body runs when next() or a for loop asks for a value, so its errors and effects can be delayed.

context-managers.question: How many times should a @contextmanager function yield?
options: Twice: once for setup and once for cleanup
context-managers.explanation: Code before the single yield acquires the resource; code after it, in finally, cleans up.

packaging-and-cli.question: argparse reads --minutes with type=int. Which value is accepted by argparse but still needs a domain check?
packaging-and-cli.explanation: int("-5") succeeds, so argparse accepts it; the rule that minutes are nonnegative is yours to check. argparse already rejects abc.

logging-and-test-design.question: Where should unittest.mock.patch replace a dependency?
options: Where the code under test looks it up
In the module that originally defined it, always
logging-and-test-design.explanation: patch replaces a name in one namespace. If the consumer imported the function into its own module, patch it there, and only for the test that needs the failure.

concurrency-models.question: In what order does ThreadPoolExecutor.map return results?
concurrency-models.explanation: map yields results in input order, even when later inputs finish first.

profiling-and-complexity.question: What does Big-O describe?
options: How cost grows as the input grows
The exact runtime on your machine
profiling-and-complexity.explanation: Big-O describes growth, not seconds. Measure real workloads to learn actual runtimes.

security-and-input-boundaries.question: Why read at most limit + 1 bytes from an input?
options: To leave room for a trailing newline
To detect oversize input without loading all of it
security-and-input-boundaries.explanation: If the extra byte arrives, the input is too large and can be rejected before a huge allocation. Checking size after reading everything is too late.

robust-storage.question: Why close the temporary file before calling os.replace?
options: Windows can refuse to replace using a file that is still open
os.replace accepts only closed file objects
robust-storage.explanation: On Windows an open file can block the replacement, and closing also ensures buffered data has been written. os.replace takes paths, not file objects.

robust-import-capstone.question: One record in a batch of 100 repeats an earlier id. What does the importer publish?
robust-import-capstone.explanation: The batch must pass every record and batch invariant before one commit, so partial success never looks like a complete import.

foundation.question: def total(minutes): sum(minutes). What does total([10, 20]) return?
foundation.explanation: The function computes the sum but never returns it, so the call produces None.

foundation.question: A user adds a record with minutes = -5 to a valid saved log. What should the program do?
options: Save it and fix it on the next load
Replace the log with an empty list
Reject it and leave the saved log unchanged
foundation.explanation: Validate before saving. An invalid record is reported and the existing log stays as it was.

foundation.question: A tuple such as ("Python", 20) is saved with json.dumps and read back with json.loads. What comes back?
foundation.explanation: JSON has arrays but no tuples, so the tuple is written as an array and read back as a list.

intermediate.question: @dataclass class Session: minutes: int. What is Session("ten").minutes?
intermediate.explanation: The annotation is not enforced at runtime. Check types yourself, for example in __post_init__.

intermediate.question: gen = (n for n in [1, 2, 3]); next(gen). What does list(gen) return now?
intermediate.explanation: A generator is one-pass. next already consumed 1, so list collects what remains.

intermediate.question: A command-line tool receives --minutes -5. What should it do?
options: Report the error and exit with a nonzero status
Print a warning and save the record
Exit with status 0 so scripts keep running
intermediate.explanation: An expected input error is reported clearly, and a nonzero status tells the caller or script that the command failed.

advanced.question: A coroutine calls time.sleep(2). What happens to the other tasks on the event loop?
options: They keep running on other threads
They wait, because the event loop is blocked
advanced.explanation: Blocking code inside a coroutine stops the event loop. Use await asyncio.sleep, or run blocking work elsewhere.

advanced.question: A new aggregation is twice as fast but returns a different result for empty input. What is it?
options: Not an optimization until the results match
An optimization with a known edge case
Acceptable, because the speedup was measured
advanced.explanation: Compare behavior on representative and edge inputs before timing; a fast wrong answer is not an improvement.

advanced.question: The importer rejects a batch. What should happen to the previous report file?
options: It is replaced with an empty report
It is deleted so stale data cannot be read
advanced.explanation: Validation happens before the write path, and replacement is atomic, so a rejected batch leaves the earlier output intact.
